Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency causes complement-mediated subcutaneous edema; episodic gut and airway swelling does not establish lasting organ damage.
Dysferlin-related dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; reduced reflexes do not establish a separate neuropathy.
Mild factor VIII deficiency defines a coagulation disorder; chronic joint damage is not common in this mild form.
Anal mucosal primary; supplied HPO reports liver, skeletal and lung neoplasms each in 30-79%, supporting metastatic occupation of these organs.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes GM2 storage and progressive juvenile neurodegeneration; damaging ocular involvement is not consistently common.
Chronic skin disease >80%, lung cysts ~75%, skeletal fragility 30-79%; frequent dental/esophageal disease and chronic otitis omitted at four-axis cap.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease; strabismus occurs in 1/2 assessed patients, supporting ocular dysfunction with limited sampling.
Acute infection and inflammation of the external ear.
Provided synonyms describe congenital progressive muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability, defining skeletal muscle and CNS disease.
Sphingolipid-biosynthesis disorder causing sensory neuropathy; trophic skin ulcers occur in 4/7; osteomyelitis in 3/5 is a separate infection.
Malignant mesenchymal tumor of soft tissues or nervous system, defined by sarcomatous and neural components.
Congenital fusion of the radius and ulna directly affects the skeleton and forearm movement.
Encephalopathy with developmental impairment and brain abnormalities; ptosis affects eyelid function in 30-79%; respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Definition specifies malignant involvement of the jaw skeleton; digestive-system ancestry alone does not establish mucosal disease.
Fuchs endothelial dystrophy directly damages the corneal endothelium and impairs vision.
Factor II coagulopathy; supplied HPO reports joint and intracranial hemorrhage each in 30-79%, supporting joint and CNS injury; epistaxis alone adds no airway damage.
Autoinflammatory immunodeficiency with glycogen storage; damaging muscle and myocardial amylopectin accumulation affect most classic reported cases (>50%).
Myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia define syndrome; intellectual disability 30-79%; glaucoma 30-79% omitted at four-axis cap.
Inherited retinal dystrophy directly damages the retina; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Limb and urethral malformations define syndrome; cardiac defects 80-99%; ureteral anomalies 30-79% reinforce renal; splenic septation does not establish dysfunction.
A disease of joints remains musculoskeletal even when temporary; an immune mechanism is not established for the umbrella.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; strabismus 3/6 and atrial septal defect 1/3 support involvement, with small samples; reflux alone lacks documented injury.
Syndromic ichthyosis defines skin disease; skeletal, neurological and endocrine abnormalities vary by subtype and are not established in most across the umbrella.
Parkinsonism and peripheral polyneuropathy directly affect the nervous system; the mitochondrial gene alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
